issues.failure_explanation: The error measure uses the scaled matrices $\bA_t = L_t \bA R_t^\top$. Thus its left term is $L_t(\Phi(Y_t)-\frac1m X_t^{-1})L_t^\top$ and its right term is $R_t(\Phi^*(X_t)-\frac1n Y_t^{-1})R_t^\top$, whereas the gradient of $f$ has components $\Phi(Y_t)-\frac1m X_t^{-1}$ and $\Phi^*(X_t)-\frac1n Y_t^{-1}$. These are generally not equal unless $L_t$ and $R_t$ are orthogonal.

failure_location.quote: It turns out that this error equals the norm of the gradient of $f$ (see~\eqref{eq: cost function}). Therefore, we call it the gradient norm.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rename the quantity as a weighted residual or state that it equals the gradient norm only when the scaling factors are orthogonal.
issues.overall_effect: The residual used in the experiments is mislabeled as the gradient norm. The numerical results still measure violation of the operator scaling conditions, but the stated identification with the gradient norm is false.
issues.title: Error measure is not the gradient norm of f
issues.why_classification: The false identification is local to the experimental error-measure description and does not invalidate any theoretical result or the numerical comparison itself.

issues.failure_explanation: From the operator scaling equations one has $\|R x_i\|^2 = 1/(k\ell_i^2)$ and $\sum_i \ell_i^2 (R x_i)(R x_i)^\top = \frac1n I_n$. To obtain $\tilde x_i=\alpha_i R x_i$ with $\sum_i \tilde x_i \tilde x_i^\top=I_n$ and $\|\tilde x_i\|^2=n/k$, one needs $\alpha_i^2=n\ell_i^2$, i.e. $\alpha_i=\sqrt n\,\ell_i$, not $\alpha_i=n\ell_i^2$. The stated norm condition $\|\tilde x_i\|_2=n/k$ is also inconsistent with $\sum_i\tilde x_i\tilde x_i^\top=I_n$ unless $k=n$; it should be squared: $\|\tilde x_i\|_2^2=n/k$.

failure_location.quote: So $P = R$ and $\alpha_i = n\ell_i^2$ yield a solution to frame scaling, and vice versa.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the norm condition by $\|\tilde x_i\|_2^2=n/k$ (or $\|\tilde x_i\|_2=\sqrt{n/k}$) and set $\alpha_i=\sqrt n\,\ell_i$.
issues.overall_effect: The stated frame-scaling problem and its claimed equivalence to the operator scaling instance are mathematically incorrect. The experiment description is unreliable, although the code may have used the corrected formulas.
issues.title: Incorrect equivalence between frame scaling and operator scaling
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short local correction of the experimental setup; no theoretical result depends on this equivalence.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
there exist sequences of orthogonal matrices $P_t$ and $Q_t$ with $P_0 = I$ and $Q_0 = I$ such that
 \[
  \bA_t^{} = P_t^{} \bar{\bA}_t^{} Q_t^\top.
 \]

issues.failure_explanation: The induction hypothesis gives $A_t = P_t \bar A_t Q_t^\top$, hence $\bar A_t = P_t^\top A_t Q_t$ and $\bar A_t \bar A_t^\top = P_t^\top A_t A_t^\top P_t$. The proof instead uses $P_t (\sum A_t A_t^\top) P_t^\top$, with the transposition reversed. This invalidates the subsequent derivation of $P_{t+1}$ and the relations between $L_{t+1}$ and $\bar L_{t+1}$ as written.

failure_location.quote: \bar C_t^{} \bar C_t^{\top} = \sum_{i=1}^k \bar A_{t,i}^{} \bar A_{t,i}^\top = P_t^{} \left( \sum_{i=1}^k A_{t,i}^{} A_{t,i}^\top \right) P_t^{\top}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $P_t$ by $P_t^\top$ in the induction-step equality (or equivalently adjust the induction hypothesis to $\bar A_t = P_t A_t Q_t^\top$) and propagate the change through the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Proposition~\ref{prop: equivalence of algorithms} is invalid as written. The proposition itself remains true and can be repaired by consistently transposing $P_t$ in the induction step.
issues.title: Transposition error in proof of Proposition equivalence
issues.why_classification: The error is a local transposition inconsistency in an auxiliary proof; a short notational correction restores the argument without changing the proposition or downstream results.
